transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Elena Torres (Redwood SE), Samir Venkatar (Redwood Solutions), Marcus Nguyen (HarborBay CTO), Aisha Roberts (Head of Search), Daniel Lee (ML Eng), Priyanka Sharma (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
HarborBay is evaluating Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints to improve search relevance for their news archive. Primary constraints: sub-100ms p99 for interactive search, cost sensitivity at scale (billions of tokens/day less likely but tens of millions queries per month), SOC2 and VPC options. They want a pilot with ~10M docs and evaluate recall vs latency trade-offs. Next steps: pricing, security docs, hands-on console demo.

Topics: onboarding, embeddings selection, rerank endpoint, batching/throughput, console walkthrough, security and compliance, pilot scope

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marcus (HarborBay): Marcus here. Hey.
[00:10] Aisha (HarborBay): Aisha, hi.
[00:12] Daniel (HarborBay): Daniel here.
[00:15] Jordan: Cool. Elena, Samir from our side?
[00:17] Elena (Redwood SE): Here. Happy to dive into the tech.
[00:20] Samir (Redwood): Yep.
[00:22] Jordan: Agenda — we want to show the hosted embeddings API, the rerank endpoint flow, then a short tour of the Redwood Console Optimize suggestions. We'll leave time for security questions.
[00:30] Marcus: Sounds good, our primary drivers are improving recall for long-tail queries and lowering misranked breaking news results. Latency is important — sub 100ms p99 for search experience.
[00:40] Aisha: Also, we have a mixed infra — core app on AWS, data long term in GCS. We need to understand VPC/private options later.
[00:48] Jordan: Great. Quick qual: how many documents and queries per second are you expecting in pilot?
[00:55] Daniel: For prototype we can start with 10M docs, index ~1.2M active. QPS — maybe 50 qps sustained during business hours, spikes to 200 qps.
[01:06] Elena: Good to know. Hosted API with our embeddings + rerank should handle that with autoscaling, but we can show you cost/latency profiles and dedicated reserved pools if you need tight p99 SLAs.
[01:16] Marcus: What's the delta between hosted and dedicated for p99 and cost?
[01:20] Jordan: In short, hosted is fastest time-to-value and scales elastically. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput and unit cost reductions — we'll send a side-by-side pricing sheet.
[01:30] Elena: I'll show the trade-offs in the console in a sec. For now, let's demo the basic pipeline: embedding upsert -> ann vector store (you can use your own Faiss/Milvus or our vector index) -> initial retrieval -> rerank via Redwood hosted rerank endpoint which runs a compact cross-encoder style reranker for better precision.
[01:48] Daniel: Wait, cross-encoder on the hosted rerank? How does that scale — are you doing full pairwise scoring?
[01:55] Elena: We do an optimized approach: initial ANN recall to ~200 candidates, then a rerank step that scores those with a small cross-encoder. We have optimizations like sharded batching and KV prefix caching so the per-query cost is controlled. Also you can configure cutoff and candidate window size in the API.
[02:10] Aisha: Can you tune the candidate window? We tried 500 and it shot up cost.
[02:14] Elena: Yes, typical pilot will use 50-200 candidates. We recommend starting at 100 and measuring the incremental precision lift vs cost. Our Optimize module gives suggestions based on query distribution.
[02:24] Jordan: I'm going to share my screen — live console. 
[02:28] [screen share] Jordan: This is the Embeddings page. First, model catalog — we surface multiple embedding models with measured dimensionality and latency. For HarborBay, for news short documents, we recommend the 768-d open model for a trade-off between compute and quality.
[02:44] Marcus: Is that an open model or Redwood-curated?
[02:47] Jordan: It's a curated open model — Redwood-verified profile with latency bench. If you need lower-cost quantized embeddings we can show quantization and smaller dims.
[02:55] Elena: Here on the Rerank endpoint demo — you can see a sample request: we pass initial candidates ids + query, and the endpoint returns a reranked list with score and explanation tokens. The explanation is probabilistic and for debugging only.
[03:10] Daniel: Do you return attention or token-level reasons? That can be noisy.
[03:13] Elena: We return a short token highlight map – lightweight. It's meant for signal, not compliance-grade explainability.
[03:20] Marcus: What about caching — prefix caching you mentioned? For searches with repeated prefixes we need low tail latency.
[03:25] Elena: Prefix KV caching stores hot KV cache entries at the runtime layer for repeated query prefixes and reduces the compute path for generation and rerank warm starts. For retrieval-heavy workloads it can reduce average latency by 15–30% depending on distribution.
[03:40] Aisha: Ok, can you show a raw API example for embeddings + rerank?
[03:45] Jordan: Yep — sample curl: 
POST /v1/embeddings upsert body... then for search: POST /v1/search with vector, top_k, return candidates, then POST /v1/rerank with candidates payload. I'll paste the example in the chat.
[03:58] Elena: Also note we support a combined search-rerank call where we accept a query and do ANN + rerank server side to reduce round trips. That endpoint is good for interactive latencies.
[04:10] Daniel: That combined call — does it impact observability? I want trace-level per-stage timing.
[04:15] Elena: We emit per-stage traces, token-level breakdown (when generation is involved), and per-route dashboards. In Console you can drill into latency waterfall — we'll show you.
[04:24] [screen share - Console traces view] Elena: Here is a latency breakdown: ANN lookup 12ms, rerank 38ms, network overhead 10ms -> p95 ~70ms for this config. Your p99 will depend on cold caches and candidate window — we show aggregated percentiles.
[04:45] Marcus: Those numbers are promising. Question on vector store: we use internal Faiss cluster on GCP; can Redwood integrate or do you force the vector index?
[04:55] Jordan: You can bring your own vector store — we have connectors for Faiss, Milvus, and Pinecone. For hosted flows most customers use our managed index to simplify ops. Integrations preserve your storage choice and we support snapshot/export for portability.
[05:10] Aisha: Security — SOC2 yes? Does hosted support tenant isolation/encryption in transit and at rest?
[05:16] Samir: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II. Hosted encrypts data in transit and at rest by default. For stronger controls we offer VPC peering options and Private deployment. KMS integrations available for dedicated/private customers. We also provide audit logs and RBAC in Console.
[05:32] Marcus: Do you allow customer-managed keys (CMK) in hosted?
[05:35] Samir: For hosted, we support bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations for dedicated/enterprise plans; full CMK in Private deployments or Dedicated with an enterprise add-on. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[05:46] Aisha: Are there data retention or PI scrubbing features? We need to redact certain fields before indexing.
[05:52] Elena: We can integrate preprocess pipelines and the Console supports transformation hooks. You can run scrubbing before upsert; we also offer in-flight token redaction for PII in some configs.
[06:04] Daniel: Back to rerank — latency wise, 38ms rerank seems optimistic. What's the model behind that? Distil cross-encoder?
[06:12] Elena: We use a compact cross-attention model optimized for rerank with kernel fusion and custom CUDA kernels; it's smaller than full cross-encoders but tuned for quality. We also offer a few variants in the model catalog — 'precision' profile and 'fast' profile.
[06:26] Marcus: Can we run an A/B between two reranker variants?
[06:29] Jordan: Absolutely — Console supports rollout policies: canary, A/B, traffic split by route, and automatic fallback. You can measure relevance metrics and automatically rollback if quality degrades.
[06:40] Aisha: What metrics do you surface for relevance? NDCG? MRR?
[06:44] Elena: NDCG@10, precision@k, recall, and you can upload your eval sets. We also support synthetic user sessions for CTR-like proxies.
[06:54] Jordan: Let's do a quick live demo with a short sample of HarborBay docs. Elena, can you load the test dataset?
[07:00] Elena: Loading now — okay, I uploaded 2k sample articles for this demo. I'll trigger search.
[07:07] [demo run — query: "storm coverage timeline"]
[07:10] Elena: Initial ANN returns 150 candidates. Rerank top results show improved ordering — note we surface the score delta between baseline and rerank.
[07:22] Aisha: Hmm I see an older piece ranked above a corrected article — can you show why?
[07:27] Elena: Explanation shows the reranker favored more recent context tokens; but date is not a first-class feature in this model — you can add metadata features or boost by date field at retrieval time.
[07:38] Daniel: So fielded search + vector similarity is still best practice.
[07:41] Elena: Yes, hybrid scoring. You can add a metadata filter in the search request to boost or exclude by date/source.
[07:48] Marcus: Any guidance on embedding dimensionality vs recall for news?
[07:52] Elena: Higher dims generally increase recall for nuanced semantics but increase index size and latency. For news, 512–768 is a good sweet spot. Optimize will recommend based on your actual query distribution.
[08:05] Jordan: Quick aside on cost: rerank is billed per candidate scored and per-token on the reranker model. We'll provide a sample cost spreadsheet.
[08:12] Marcus: Could we do k-nearest offline to precompute rerank candidates for hot queries?
[08:17] Elena: Yes — you can precompute for top queries, use caching at CDN level, or use our TTL-based cache on the index. Precomputation is common for top-funnel queries.
[08:29] Aisha: How do we measure query drift or model regressions?
[08:33] Elena: Console Optimize includes regression alerts tied to eval sets and live query cohorts. You set thresholds and it will trigger a regression alert + suggested rollback.
[08:42] Marcus: For the pilot, what do you recommend for dataset partitioning and rollout?
[08:47] Jordan: Start with a shadow index — run rerank in shadow for a few days to collect metrics, then a canary at 5–10% traffic, expand to 50% if metrics look good. We'll help set up the eval suite.
[08:58] Daniel: About observability — do we get token-level cost breakdown per request?
[09:02] Elena: Yes, Console shows token-level and per-route cost. You can set cost alerts and per-team quotas.
[09:10] [short pause — background noise]
[09:14] Priyanka (HarborBay): Quick question — onboarding time, how fast until we can run the pilot?
[09:18] Jordan: Technically you can be up in a day for a basic hosted flow. For the full security review and reserved capacity, expect 2–3 weeks for procurement and setup.
[09:28] Marcus: Procurement and SSO are blockers for us. We use Okta and need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[09:34] Samir: We support SAML/Okta and SCIM. We'll send the integration guide.
[09:40] Aisha: Are you able to sign an MSSA or standard enterprise contract?
[09:43] Jordan: Yes — AE will loop in legal.
[09:46] Marcus: Great. Back to technical — what about embedding drift over time? If we update the model, how to keep vectors backward compatible?
[09:54] Elena: You can pin model versions per index; Redwood supports migrations and you can run backfills. We also offer quantization profiles and documentation for incremental reindexing. Versioning is first-class in the Console.
[10:06] Daniel: For reindexing 10M docs, what's typical duration?
[10:09] Elena: Depends on throughput; with dedicated pool we can do tens of thousands docs/min. For hosted, it's elastic but you should plan hours to a day depending on size and attachments.
[10:20] Marcus: Is there a way to stage the reindex to avoid a big cost spike?
[10:24] Jordan: Yes — incremental backfills and throttling policies. You can also do hybrid approaches where you keep old vectors for cold docs.
[10:33] Aisha: Any specific pitfalls you see for news publishers?
[10:37] Elena: Two things: (1) temporal relevance — inject time/features at retrieval, and (2) entity disambiguation — consider domain-specific fine-tuning or metadata signals.
[10:46] Daniel: Does Redwood offer fine-tuning for rerankers?
[10:49] Elena: We offer a model onboarding path — you can bring annotated pairs and we can fine-tune private reranker variants for higher precision on your domain, usually as part of dedicated/private engagements.
[10:59] Marcus: Ok. Can you run a short QPS stress to simulate spikes?
[11:03] Jordan: We can, but let's schedule a benchmark run. I'll propose a time in the follow-up.
[11:08] Aisha: That'd be great — we want to test 200 qps spikes.
[11:12] Elena: We'll include sample load scripts and how to interpret the traces.
[11:17] Marcus: Compliance again — do you have a fedramp plan?
[11:20] Samir: Not currently FedRAMP, but Private deployments for regulated customers are possible. For now we meet SOC2 and ISO controls for enterprise.
[11:30] Jordan: Wrapping into Console Optimize — here's the Optimize page which suggests candidate window sizes, quantization settings, and batching policies based on your observed distribution. You can apply a recommended profile with one click in staging.
[11:45] Aisha: Apply one-click is nice. Does it do dry-run?
[11:48] Elena: It simulates impact and shows projected cost delta and expected p95/p99 change before applying.
[11:54] Daniel: Great. What's the pilot success criteria we should agree on?
[11:58] Jordan: Proposed success metrics: NDCG@10 improvement +8% over baseline, p99 latency <= 120ms for the combined call, and cost per 1k queries under an agreed threshold. If those are met during a 2-week canary we'll move to reserved capacity discussions.
[12:16] Marcus: That seems reasonable.
[12:18] Priyanka: Who will be our main contacts for execution?
[12:21] Jordan: Jordan AE for project, Elena SE for technical run, Samir for security and procurement. We'll coordinate with Daniel for dataset and infra.
[12:30] Marcus: Ok let's do it.
[12:33] [wrap-up section] Jordan: Recap — we'll send pilot pricing and the security pack, schedule the hands-on Console workshop (60m) with your ML Eng next week, and set up a benchmark window for the 200 qps spike. Action items captured in the meeting notes.
[12:49] Aisha: Thanks all.
[12:50] Daniel: Thanks.
[12:51] Marcus: Appreciate it.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
